newsitem.title: USA: CalEnergy says well set to pursue NYSEG.
newsitem.headline: CalEnergy says well set to pursue NYSEG.

text.p: CalEnergy Co Inc said Tuesday it was committed to a takeover of New York State Electric and Gas Corp and would pursue more aggressive steps if the target did not agree to a friendly transaction.

In a conference call with analysts, CalEnergy Chairman David Sokol said the independent power producer has $2 billion in financing committed for a transaction and will pursue a proxy fight or consent solicitation if necessary.
"We at CalEnergy finish what we start," he said.

CalEnergy anticipates it will take nine to 12 months to complete a hostile takeover, he said. Due to various regulatory approvals needed, that timeframe would be shortened only slightly in the event of a friendly deal.
Sokol also said a transaction with NYSEG would likely require CalEnergy to divest five percent of its generating capacity.
CalEnergy earlier announced it was launching a tender offer of $24.50 per share for 6.5 million NYSEG shares as the first step in a plan to take over the utility.
Together with NYSEG shares it already ownes, the tender would give CalEnergy a 9.9 stake in the company.
CalEnergy also said it would pay $27.50 per share in a friendly deal.
Shares of NYSEG jumped 2-13/16 to 24-3/16 in morning trade. CalEnergy dipped 11/16 to 38-7/8.
Sokol said CalEnergy already owns about 240,000 shares of NYSEG.
Although he declined to specifically discuss a deal's impact on earnings. he noted that CalEnergy's deals typically do not inhibit net income or earnings.
